Class MEditor

java.lang.Object
android.view.View
android.widget.TextView
android.widget.EditText
net.murat.uikit.MEditor
All Implemented Interfaces:
android.graphics.drawable.Drawable.Callback, android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityEventSource, android.view.KeyEvent.Callback, android.view.ViewTreeObserver.OnPreDrawListener
public class MEditor extends android.widget.EditText
Multi-line editor with: - a fast-scroll strip on the right edge (linear mapping of touch Y to scroll position), - drag scrolling with fling, implemented on top of the native EditText scroll, - a "first tap" focus guard so the keyboard does not pop up unexpectedly, - an external read-only mode.

Touch behavior (normal EditText feel, but robust against finger drift): - Short tap: the caret is placed at the touched position. - Press and hold (finger stays within touch slop): the word under the finger is selected; dragging afterwards extends the selection (handled by EditText). - Finger moves beyond touch slop before the long-press fires: the pending long-press is cancelled, so no word gets selected; only scrolling/fling happens.

    • setEditorText

      public void setEditorText(String fullText)
      Replaces the whole editor content and moves the caret to the start.

      This is the "fresh document" variant used by file-open flows and anywhere the caller explicitly wants the caret at 0. For in-place edits that should keep the user near where they were, call setEditorText(String, boolean) with preserveCaret=true.

    • setEditorText

      public void setEditorText(String fullText, boolean preserveCaret)
      Replaces the whole editor content.

      When preserveCaret is true, the caret is kept near its previous position (clamped to the new length). When false, the caret is moved to the start — matching the historical behavior of setEditorText(String).

      Both variants reset the first-tap focus guard so the next tap behaves as the "first tap" for the new content.

    • setText

      public void setText(CharSequence text, android.widget.TextView.BufferType type)
      Overrides EditText's content setter to preserve the caret position (and collapsed selection anchor) across content swaps.

      Behavior:

      • When preserveCaretOnSetText is false, behaves exactly like the superclass (caret ends up wherever the framework puts it, typically 0 for fresh content).
      • When true, the current selection start is remembered, the content is swapped, and then the caret is restored to min(savedPos, newLength). Any active selection is collapsed to the caret — we do not attempt to restore the anchor because the two ends may no longer correspond to the same text after a transformation.

      Must run on the main thread (all EditText mutations do).

      Overrides:
      setText in class android.widget.EditText
